principles.principle: Separate public website access from authenticated product access.
examples: A public visitor can read service descriptions.
An authenticated user may access restricted functionality only after authorization.

principles.description: Knowing who a user is does not automatically establish which records or actions they may access.
Give each role only the access required for its confirmed responsibilities.
Caregiver, guardian, proxy, or representative access must follow the organization's verified authorization and consent rules.

principles.principle: Separate read, create, update, approve, export, and delete permissions.
principles.description: These actions must not be treated as equivalent.

principles.principle: Require explicit review for high-impact actions.

principles.description: For protected systems, define how permissions are granted, checked, changed, reviewed, and revoked.

agent_constraints: Do not invent the customer's role-permission matrix.
Do not infer access from a job title alone.
Do not expose protected information in public website content.
Do not implement access-control behavior based solely on a generated persona.
Require customer and security review before finalizing sensitive permissions.
